credit_metrics.text: Revenue was broadly unchanged at {{revenue@FY2025}}, but EBITDA fell by {{ebitda.change@FY2025}} to {{ebitda@FY2025}} and the EBITDA margin narrowed by {{ebitda_margin.change@FY2025}} to {{ebitda_margin@FY2025}}.

Total debt was reduced by {{total_debt.change@FY2025}} to {{total_debt@FY2025}}, yet gross leverage rose by {{gross_leverage.change@FY2025}} to {{gross_leverage@FY2025}} as EBITDA declined by {{ebitda.change@FY2025}}.
Interest coverage improved by {{interest_coverage.change@FY2025}} to {{interest_coverage@FY2025}}, still below the peer median.

FFO declined by {{ffo.change@FY2025}} to {{ffo@FY2025}}, taking FFO to debt down by {{ffo_to_debt.change@FY2025}} to {{ffo_to_debt@FY2025}}, and FCF to debt fell by {{fcf_to_debt.change@FY2025}} to {{fcf_to_debt@FY2025}}.

Operating profit fell by {{operating_profit.change@FY2025}} to {{operating_profit@FY2025}}, and capex intensity eased by {{capex_intensity.change@FY2025}} to {{capex_intensity@FY2025}}, below the peer median.

peer_positioning.text: Finnair has the weakest EBITDA margin of the network peers ({{ebitda_margin.peer_rank@2025}}), at {{ebitda_margin@FY2025}} against a median of {{ebitda_margin.peer_median@2025}}.

Gross leverage of {{gross_leverage@FY2025}} is above the peer median of {{gross_leverage.peer_median@2025}} and ranks {{gross_leverage.peer_rank@2025}}, while net leverage of {{net_leverage@FY2025}} sits in line with the median.

Cash generation trails the group: FFO to debt of {{ffo_to_debt@FY2025}} is below the peer median of {{ffo_to_debt.peer_median@2025}} and ranks {{ffo_to_debt.peer_rank@2025}}, while FCF to debt of {{fcf_to_debt@FY2025}} places the company in the middle of the group ({{fcf_to_debt.peer_rank@2025}}).
Liquidity is the relative strength: cash liquidity to revenue of {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue@FY2025}} is the highest of the group ({{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.peer_rank@2025}}).

snapshot.text: Finnair, the Finnish network carrier, closed FY2025 with a weaker earnings profile, as prolonged industrial action in the first half and environmental regulation and navigation charges weighed on the result, leaving the EBITDA margin at {{ebitda_margin@FY2025}}.
Net leverage fell by {{net_leverage.change@FY2025}} to {{net_leverage@FY2025}}, in line with the peer median, as net debt was reduced by {{net_debt.change@FY2025}} to {{net_debt@FY2025}}.

The point to watch is cash generation: FFO to debt fell by {{ffo_to_debt.change@FY2025}} to {{ffo_to_debt@FY2025}}, below the peer median, with free cash flow down {{fcf.change@FY2025}} to {{fcf@FY2025}}.

watch_items.text: Cash generation: FFO to debt of {{ffo_to_debt@FY2025}} is below the peer median of {{ffo_to_debt.peer_median@2025}}, and FCF to debt fell by {{fcf_to_debt.change@FY2025}} to {{fcf_to_debt@FY2025}}.
Margins: the EBITDA margin narrowed by {{ebitda_margin.change@FY2025}} to {{ebitda_margin@FY2025}}, the weakest of the network peers ({{ebitda_margin.peer_rank@2025}}).

Leverage: gross leverage rose by {{gross_leverage.change@FY2025}} to {{gross_leverage@FY2025}}, above the peer median of {{gross_leverage.peer_median@2025}}, so the fall in net leverage of {{net_leverage.change@FY2025}} rests on the reduction in net debt of {{net_debt.change@FY2025}} rather than on earnings.

Cost base: the fuel share of costs of {{fuel_share_of_costs@FY2025}} is above the peer median of {{fuel_share_of_costs.peer_median@2025}}, and environmental regulation costs weighed on the result during the year.
